newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse dips on Nafta losses.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse dips on Nafta losses.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) continued in slugish trading and downward trend on Friday, with losses to Nafta share driving the the SAX index down 0.48 points to 189.84.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed down 22 crowns at 1,830, trading only 20 stocks on the BSE floor, and brokers said they sceptical over its future development.
"At present, the demand for Nafta shares is very low and this may drag its price further down in near future," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.

Steel maker VSZ led today's trading on the BSE floor with 1,464 shares changing hands, closing unchanged at 605 crowns. Brokers described VZS as the only blue chips with the potential to significantly increase in near future.
"VSZ now seems to be the best stock among the blue chips, as it is fundamentally a good company, and I expect a significant increase in its price in near future," Sykora said.
Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB closed up seven crowns to 1,645. Oil refiner Slovnaft did not trade on Friday.
Overall volume decreased to 215,626 shares, from 544,070 traded on Thursday, and turnover fell to 156.98 million crowns from 358.87 million. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newswroom, 42-7-563-3687
